summary: ```markdown # CLO Skill Workshop - Hair Obstruction and Seam Treatment Methods ## Introduction This time, the technique class will talk about how to deal with hair blocking. When combing, if it is a style similar to a belt that covers the hair belt, then there will be a phenomenon of hair passing through the belt. Additionally, at the seam, it is necessary to achieve the effect of the hair being pressed by the sewing line. In this issue, I will discuss the processing techniques involved. ## Choosing the Fixing Needle Tool First of all, we choose the fixing needle tool. In the 3D window, with an empty selection, this step is to find the part of the belt covering the clothing. Once we add the fixing needle, you can see the marks that the fixing needle adds on the 2D board. The gap in the middle represents the part of the belt covering. ## Drawing the Basic Line Next, we can select our basic line tool and draw the basic line on it. This line will outline the range of our blocking, making it more convenient for us to fill in the blanks later. While drawing, press the Ctrl key and the left-click button to create a curve line. ## Printing the Fabric After adding the curve line, we can switch to print mode. Here, we need to find the fabric of the jacket. We can then pour out the fabric of our jacket. At this point, we only need to display the basic line, as the hair has no texture. Therefore, we can choose the fabric texture directly to display the entire version in pure color. ## Saving the Work Next, we check the information; this side does not need to be selected. Then, click Save. ## Editing in Photoshop Now, we open our picture in Photoshop (PS). We can see that the gap in the middle is the part of the belt covering. We will select this part and then fill it in. By adding a new layer, we can fill it in black, creating a dense default picture. In this setup, there will be no hair in the black area, while hair will be present in the white area. All layers will be displayed in one layer, with a beefile in the top layer. ## Layer Adjustments Pressing the Ctrl key allows us to start a new layer. We will look for one layer here. Most of the layers will be black. If we select this layer, we can see that the color is white. We can utilize this layer with white while selecting layers that are all black. ## Adjusting Width and Pressure Marks The width of the side can be adjusted accordingly based on the desired effect. This way, we can create an area on the edge of the board where there will be no hair inside, resulting in a pressure mark effect. Simultaneously, we can address the area without the seal, which is the collar, by wiping off the side. ## Processing Other Parts In the same way, this process can be carried out in other parts of the garment. Once the processing is complete, a default picture will resemble the desired outcome. ## Finalizing the Costume Finally, let’s revisit this costume. We will choose the large fabric and open it in the default picture. The default picture we just created will be placed into the density column. The hair density of the black area will be zero, ensuring there is no hair, while the white area will maintain the original hair density. This processing technique effectively creates the appearance of hair being blocked by the belt. ## Conclusion Next, we can examine the side seam of the clothes, where the hair pressure mark effect will also be visible. Today's class concludes here. Thank you all for your participation! ```
